title: coalesce-strategies-field-diary
content:
Status: working notes + field diary for coalescer strategy experiments. Put here because the idea drifted from earlier batch-scheduler notebooks; want a compact narrative record.

Goal: evaluate small set of coalescing heuristics that change how the runtime groups inflight tokens into GPU-friendly slices while preserving per-client latency SLOs and avoiding long tail amplification. Primary knobs: max_coalesce_size (tokens), per-request timeout_ms, urgency weights (per-tenant), client isolation (soft quotas), and early-flush heuristics for age-heavy requests.

Hardware and model baseline:
- Cluster: 2x A100:40G (worker), 1x control node (m5.large emulation).
- Model: quantized LLaMA-variant ~7B, typical generation length 32 tokens.
- Serving runtime build: main@2024-10-31 + coalescer-experiments branch.
- Workload generator: local synthetic harness (burst+poisson mixed) + replay traces from prod-shadow (Nov week).

Instrumentation used:
- pprof CPU profiles for scheduler thread.
- eBPF socket latency histogram (lightweight sampling at accept/send).
- Jaeger traces (request enter -> coalesce -> dispatch -> first-token -> stream-end).
- Custom coalesce metrics exported to Prom: batch_size_hist, batch_age_ms, eviction_count, per-tenant_delay_ms.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- M1: baseline (max_coalesce_size=512 tokens, timeout=5ms, fairness off).
- M2: shrink size (256), timeout=3ms, fairness off.
- M3: shrink size, timeout=3ms, fairness: weighted urgency (tenants A/B/C weights 1/2/3).
- M4: shrink size, timeout=6ms, add age-priority bump for requests waiting > 40ms.
- M5: dynamic_max_size: adjust max_coalesce_size based on GPU-queue-length heuristic.

Quick observations (first pass):
- Baseline M1 showed best raw throughput but worst p99 tail under mixed bursts: p50=12ms, p95=48ms, p99=212ms. Tail events correlate with a few large coalesced batches that experienced serialization + KV cache pressure.
- Shrinking coalesce size (M2) lowered p99 to ~130ms at a ~10% throughput loss; more deterministic batching reduced serialization contention.
- Weighted urgency (M3) reduced high-priority tenant p95 by ~25% but amplified mid-priority p99 (tenant B p99 jumped from 120->205ms). Need fairness metric rather than simple weight tuning.
- Age-priority bump (M4) smoothed the extreme tails: p99 fell to ~95ms across tenants, p95 stable. However, average latency rose ~6ms due to more frequent early flushes.
- Dynamic_max_size (M5) is promising: during high queue-length, coalesce size reduced automatically; when stable, it expanded for throughput. Observed lower tail with <5% throughput regression vs M1. Needs stability guard rails.

Profiling notes / bottlenecks found:
- Scheduler thread: hotspots in coalesce_slice_serialization() and kv_cache_lock contention (seen in pprof flamegraph). Large batches hold kv_cache_lock for the decode start which stalls small batches behind them.
- Network poll loop: eBPF shows occasional 200-400us spikes at send() for big responses; happens when coalesced batch leads to a larger single socket write. Consider sharding writes or splitting streaming chunks earlier.
- GPU kernel stalls not dominant here (99% GPU busy was steady). Bottleneck is in host-side serialization + lock contention.

New metrics to add (actionable):
- per-tenant_jain_index: compute fairness of latencies across tenants over sliding window.
- kv_lock_hold_ms histogram by batch_size_bucket.
- early_flush_penalty_tokens: tokens sent due to early flushes (helps cost calculus).

Hypotheses and targeted tests:
H1: Large coalesced batches increase lock hold time linearly -> causes convoying of small urgent requests. Test: instrument kv_cache_lock hold time and artificially throttle large-batch lock sections (yield points).
H2: Early flush with age bump gives better percentile SLAs for mixed-urgency traffic at modest throughput cost. Test: run A/B export on prod-shadow with age thresholds 25/40/60ms.
H3: Dynamic_max_size needs hysteresis to avoid oscillation under sawtooth load. Test: add dampening (min-window 200ms).

Experiment detail: adversarial microburst replay
- Setup: 30s warmup, then 10s microburst (200 req/s targeting tenant C), followed by 50s steady at 25req/s. Repeat 6 cycles.
- M1 result: massive tail during microburst, mean token-per-second throughput spiked, p99 across cycle ~300ms.
- M4 result: during bursts, age-bump prevented queue accumulation; p99 ~110ms, but throughput dropped 8%.

Fairness math (quick sketch):
- Use Jain's fairness index on 95th percentiles across tenants over window W: J = (sum(xi))^2 / (n * sum(xi^2)), where xi = tenant_i_p95_delay_ms normalized to [0,1]. Goal > 0.85 across our test sets.
- For M3 naive weighting, J dropped to 0.63 (bad). M4 returned ~0.86. M5 stabilized around 0.81 with hysteresis.

Runbook items / TODOs:
- [ ] Add kv_lock_hold_ms hist to prometheus and create Grafana panel overlaying batch_size. Owner: Noah. ETA: 2025-01-10.
- [ ] Prototype yield-point inside kv cache critical section; measure false-positive stalling. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2025-01-15.
- [ ] Implement hysteresis in dynamic_max_size controller (min_window_ms, cooldown). Owner: Ruth. ETA: 2025-01-22.
- [ ] Schedule prod-shadow run of M4 vs M5 (A/B) with SLO watch. Ops owner: SRE. Target: Jan 27 2025.
- [ ] Investigate splitting large socket writes into smaller chunks to reduce eBPF send spikes. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2025-02-05.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Are we over-optimizing for p99 at the cost of p50 for low-priority tenants? Product has asked that p95 is primary SLO, p99 bonus. Maybe optimize for p95 fairness and bounded p99 veto for any tenant.
- Cost impact: early flushes increase per-token overhead. Need to quantify in cost per 1M tokens. Quick back-of-envelope suggests +3–7% unit cost. Add exact counters.
- How do these heuristics interplay with kv cache warm/cold behavior for long-chained chats (100+ tokens)? Our tests used 32 token gen; need longer-run replays.

Appendix: example Jaeger trace id placeholders for curious readers:
- trace: d5e8a9c4 - M1 big-coalesce-case (span shows coalesce_wait 44ms, kv_lock_hold 28ms)
- trace: b2f6c11a - M4 age-bump success (span shows early_flush triggered at 42ms)

If meeting: suggest 30m sync with SRE + product to align on: (1) acceptable p95 fairness thresholds, (2) cost budget for early-flush, (3) rollout plan for M5 dynamic controller behind feature flag.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc minimal — link to the longer bench notebooks in linked_artifacts. We'll convert strong hypotheses into FRs once we have A/B prod-shadow results.

End of diary entry (timestamp: 2025-01-20).
